messages.author: 9c61751d797b50a0
messages.subject: Random starts in lavaan
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to sort out how to code random starts in lavaan. I've begun here:

l <- rnorm(1, 1, sd = .5)
psi <- rnorm(1, .75, sd = .5)
phi_ii <- rnorm(1, .5, sd = .25)

#-----------------------------------------------------
# Programming random starts
m5 <- 'f1 =~ 1*v1 + start(l)*v2 + start(l)*v3 + start(l)*v4
       f2 =~ 1*v5 + start(l)*v6 + start(l)*v7 + start(l)*v8
'
# Fit the m1 model
fitm5 <- cfa(m5, data = sim2fac, do.fit = FALSE)
inspect(fitm5, what = "start")
#-----------------------------------------------------

But I see that m5 does not call the value in l. What's the trick to get the lavaan object for model syntax to refer to another R object?

Thanks!
Leslie

So that you can have a reproducible example, here is the code I used to simulate the data for the model

set.seed(56566)

#Correlation matrix
Sigma <- matrix( 
  c(1  , 0.40, 0.40, 0.35, 0.10, 0.15, 0.05, 0.10, 
    0.40, 1  , 0.30, 0.40, 0.05, 0.08, 0.10, 0.05,  
    0.40, 0.30, 1  , 0.50, 0.05, 0.08, 0.10, 0.05,
    0.35, 0.40, 0.50,   1, 0.10, 0.15, 0.05, 0.10,
    0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.10,   1, 0.35, 0.45, 0.55, 
    0.15, 0.08, 0.08, 0.15, 0.35,   1, 0.40, 0.50, 
    0.05, 0.10, 0.10, 0.05, 0.45, 0.40,   1, 0.45,
    0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.10, 0.55, 0.50, 0.45, 1
    ), 
  nrow=8, 
  ncol=8)

Sigma

is.positive.definite(Sigma)

#Producing a samples from the specified multivariate normal distribution

sim2fac <- rmvnorm(750, mean = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0), sigma = Sigma) #with specified means of variables
head(sim2fac)
colnames(sim2fac) <- c("v1", "v2", "v3", "v4", "v5", "v6", "v7", "v8")

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Random starts in lavaan
parts:
The lavaan environment does not read variables from the R environment. (This seems like afeature, not a bug, to me. It would be very weird if this worked - you name a variable and it starts to be used in lavaan).

You could use (something like) the sprintf() function to build your model and insert the values.  Example below:

l <- rnorm(1, 1, sd = .5)
psi <- rnorm(1, .75, sd = .5)
phi_ii <- rnorm(1, .5, sd = .25)

#-----------------------------------------------------
# Programming random starts

m5 <- sprintf('f1 =~ 1*v1 + start(%f)*v2 + start(%f)*v3 + start(%f)*v4
       f2 =~ 1*v5 + start(%f)*v6 + start(%f)*v7 + start(%f)*v8', l, l, l, l, l, l)


Now the start values are in the model:

> m5
[1] "f1 =~ 1*v1 + start(1.431668)*v2 + start(1.431668)*v3 + start(1.431668)*v4\n       f2 =~ 1*v5 + start(1.431668)*v6 + start(1.431668)*v7 + start(1.431668)*v8

Jeremy

messages.subject: Re: Random starts in lavaan
parts:
Leslie,
  Personally, I find it easier and less error prone to work with the parameter table instead of pasting together model syntax.



HS.model <- '
  visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  visual ~~ 1*visual
  x1 ~~ x1
  x2 ~~ x2
  x3 ~~ x3
' # End Model Syntax

HS.partable <- lavaanify(HS.model)
HS.partable # unaltered parameter table

randomLambdas <- runif(3, .1, .7)
HS.partable$ustart[1:3] <- randomLambdas
HS.partable # altered parameter table

fit <- cfa(HS.partable, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit)


Keith
